question: Who among the following has given extraordinary powers during an emergency?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The President.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **President of India: **

 
 
• **Under the Constitution of India, the President can declare a national emergency if the security of India is threatened by war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.**
 
• During a national emergency, the President has the power to suspend certain fundamental rights, suspend the operation of the Parliament, and direct the states to act according to the instructions of the central government.
 
• This power has been used in response to a variety of crises, including the 1962 Sino-Indian War, the 1971 Indo-Pakistani War, and the 1975 Emergency.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister of India:-**

 
 
• It is the head of the government of India.
 
• He or she is the chief executive of the Union and the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Prime Minister is appointed by the President of India and must command the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of India:-**
 
 
• CJI is the head of the Supreme Court of India, the highest court in the country.
 
• He or she is also the head of the Indian judicial system.
 
• The CJI is appointed by the President of India on the recommendation of the Prime Minister and the Collegium of Judges.
 
 
 
• **Governor:-**
 
 
• The Governor of a state in India is the constitutional head of the state.
 
• They are appointed by the president of India and hold office for a term of five years.
 
• The governor is responsible for upholding the constitution and the law in the state.
